title: Intraspecific sequence variation and complete genomes refine the identification of rapidly evolved regions in humans.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the bioRxiv preprint full text (PMC12633414) via Europe PMC: data statement, methods, assay library composition. Fetched the Lowe lab website: only the 2022 HAQER (human ancestor quickly evolved region) data page exists; no page or files for the 2026 Consensus HAQER set were linked from the homepage. Europe PMC found no PMCID, supplement or GEO link for the published version.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 1,596 Consensus HAQERs from a 20-way T2T (telomere-to-telomere) alignment; scSTARR-seq (single-cell enhancer reporter assay) tested only 8 HAQER inserts (75-insert library) in mouse brain (12,435 cells after QC) and 8 in human cardiomyocytes (5,648 cells); preprint said data 'will be' posted to the lab site and GEO at publication.

a1_downloadable.note: Consensus HAQER files not found on the lab site or in GEO via NCBI links; preprint only promised deposition at publication. Not verified downloadable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only measured outcome (enhancer activity) exists for 8 regions. A 'is a HAQER' label would be a computed annotation, not a measurement.

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequences would come from public genome assemblies (hs1/CHM13) by coordinate; from paper text only.

a4_units_stated.note: Enhancer activity is a normalized RNA/DNA ratio relative to scrambled controls (paper text).

a5_enough_rows.note: 8 HAQERs assayed per scSTARR-seq experiment; 1,596 regions total have no measured label.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Region set is small; alignments (multi-GB) would not be needed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable in files; preprint and published abstract both state 1,596 regions.

a8_label_provenance.note: HAQER status is computed from inter-species sequence divergence, so predicting it from sequence/alignment features is circular by construction.

existing_models.name: Whalen et al. 2023 (Neuron), machine-learning dissection of human accelerated regions using Sei and lentiMPRA
existing_models.score_and_split: Scored human vs chimpanzee HAR (human accelerated region) variants with Sei (a deep sequence-to-chromatin model) and validated against MPRA (massively parallel reporter assay) in neural progenitors; not HAQER-specific.

integration.partner_dataset: ENCODE cCREs or Lowe-lab HAQER MPRA from the companion cortical-development preprint
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence-to-function models predict which rapidly evolved human regions gained enhancer activity? Not answerable here with 8 assayed regions.

controls.positive_control: Scrambled negative-control constructs in the assay (paper)
controls.negative_control: Random neutral region set (hs1 RAND) defined by the authors

honest_claim_h3: With 8 assayed regions, no model claim is possible; only zero-shot scoring of 1,596 computed regions against a handful of measurements.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence of rapidly evolved human regions to predict whether each acts as an enhancer in developing brain or heart.
plain_idea.train_on: DNA sequences of Consensus HAQERs; only 8 have a measured enhancer activity (from paper text).
plain_idea.predict: Enhancer activity from a single-cell reporter assay (reporter RNA over input DNA, relative to scrambled controls).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would prioritise which human-specific regions to test experimentally, but there are far too few measurements to train or even evaluate a model.

ml_idea: Zero-shot score Consensus HAQERs with a sequence-to-function model and compare to the 8 scSTARR-seq measurements; too small to be a project.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; project rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count regions with measured enhancer activity: 8 per assay (paper text).

verdict_reason: Evolutionary annotation paper: the 1,596-region set is computed from sequence divergence (circular as a label), only 8 regions have measured enhancer activity, and the Consensus HAQER files were not found online.
